# API

**Team draft target:** REST + JSON under `/api/`, built with Django REST Framework. The OpenAPI schema is generated by drf-spectacular at `/api/schema/` (browsable docs at `/api/docs/`), and the front end uses TypeScript types generated from it (`pnpm gen:api`). CI fails when the committed types differ from the schema.

## Implementation status

This document publishes the team draft supplied for SET-15 (#406). The
conventions are the team's API contract; they are not a claim that every rule
or endpoint is implemented. The endpoint catalog retains the draft's methods,
paths, roles, and purposes, with a separate status column.

Status refers to the current working tree, not a deployed release:

- **Implemented:** the endpoint and its response are present. The health check
  is a plain Django view returning JSON; it is described in OpenAPI without
  changing its implementation.
- **Partial:** framework routing exists, but the complete authentication
  contract and workflows listed in the draft have not been verified by SET-15.
- **Planned:** no corresponding application endpoint is registered in this
  checkout. The listed role and purpose describe intended behavior.

The infrastructure endpoints `/api/schema/` and `/api/docs/` are implemented.
In production, both require an authenticated, active Iris `admin` role; the
application role is checked independently of Django's `is_staff` flag. They stay
public with local/test settings for developer tooling. Schema generation through
`manage.py spectacular` remains available without an HTTP session.
The schema describes health and implemented DRF endpoints, including `/api/me/`,
categories and invitation acceptance; it does not describe allauth operations,
the staging-only readiness probe, or planned business APIs.
`pnpm gen:api` produces the generated declarations, and the existing CI workflow
is configured to reject missing or outdated generated types. See the
[generation guide](../guides/api-generation.md).

The current frontend health consumer still declares its own `HealthResponse`
and validates responses at runtime. Generated types are available; existing
consumers have not been rewritten to use them.

Categories were added by
[reference module #377](https://github.com/B-A-D-R-SL/iris/issues/377).

### Production request limits (FIX-04 / SEC-04)

Production applies DRF anonymous and authenticated request limits, initially
**60/minute per anonymous client IP** and **300/minute per authenticated account**.
Operators configure these with `DRF_ANON_THROTTLE_RATE` and
`DRF_USER_THROTTLE_RATE`. The partner application endpoint retains its existing
**5/hour/IP** limit shared by anonymous and signed-in callers. Allauth keeps its
separate sign-in protection; the plain Django health and staging readiness probes
are not DRF-throttled.

An exceeded DRF limit returns HTTP 429 with
`{"code": "throttled", "message": "…", "fields": {}}` and `Retry-After`.
Messages follow the request language. DRF's cache-based limits are best effort
under concurrency. Trust forwarded client addresses only after setting the
verified `DRF_NUM_PROXIES`; changing connection ports does not create an allowance.
See [production settings](../guides/production-settings.md) for proxy and cache
requirements. DRF permission checks run before throttling: repeated anonymous
requests to a protected route return 401 without consuming its DRF quota.

Allauth's login action instead returns HTTP 429 with `{"status": 429}` and no
`Retry-After`. Failed-credential lockouts use HTTP 400 with an
`errors[].code` of `too_many_login_attempts`. These responses bypass the DRF
handler. See [authentication routing](../guides/auth-routing.md#rate-limit-responses)
for the browser behavior and allauth's separate trusted-proxy setting.

## Conventions

| Topic       | Rule                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Paths       | Plural nouns, kebab-case, trailing slash: `/api/partner-applications/`. Area prefixes: none (household), `/api/store/` (store staff), `/api/staff/` (intake workers and admins) |
| Actions     | Verbs only for state changes that are not plain updates: `POST /api/staff/partner-applications/{id}/approve/`                                                                   |
| Ids         | UUID strings                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Dates       | ISO 8601 with time zone, in UTC in the API (`2026-10-21T20:00:00Z`); shown in America/Montreal time on screen                                                                   |
| Money       | Integer cents in fields ending with `_cents`                                                                                                                                    |
| Paging      | `?page=1&page_size=20` (max 100); response `{ "count", "next", "previous", "results" }`                                                                                         |
| Errors      | HTTP status + `{ "code": "validation_error", "message": "...", "fields": { "postal_code": ["Enter a postal code like H2X 1Y4"] } }`; messages in the user's language            |
| Auth        | Session cookie (django-allauth headless) + CSRF token header `X-CSRFToken`                                                                                                      |
| Permissions | Checked on the server for every endpoint; deny by default. `backend/tests/test_endpoint_access.py` (SEC-05) calls every DRF endpoint as each role, and every DRF endpoint not listed as public anonymously, and checks that DRF's permission check lets the request through or refuses it. Plain Django routes under `/api/` (health, allauth) are listed with a reason but not called. The role matrix comes with US-07 (#434) |
| Languages   | `Accept-Language: fr` or `en`                                                                                                                                                   |

## Endpoints

### Health and reference data

| Method         | Path                     | Who    | Purpose            | Status      |
| -------------- | ------------------------ | ------ | ------------------ | ----------- |
| GET            | `/api/health/`           | Anyone | `{"status": "ok"}` | Implemented |
| GET/HEAD       | `/api/ready/`            | Anyone (no session) | Staging readiness: database connectivity, worker process and release revision | Implemented (staging only) |
| GET            | `/api/categories/`       | Anyone | Active categories  | Implemented |
| GET/POST       | `/api/staff/categories/` | Admin  | List every category (active or not); add one | Implemented (US-35) |
| PATCH          | `/api/staff/categories/{code}/` | Admin | Rename, change food or default value, deactivate or reactivate; no delete | Implemented (US-35) |

`/api/ready/` is a public plain Django view registered only by
`iris.settings.staging` through `iris.staging_urls`. It accepts GET and HEAD and
disables caching. It reads the supervised worker PID from `/run/iris/worker.pid`,
requires a PID greater than one and checks that process exists with
`os.kill(pid, 0)`, then executes database `SELECT 1`. Success returns HTTP 200;
GET includes `{"status": "ok", "revision": "<IRIS_RELEASE_SHA>"}` (revision defaults
to `local` when unset). A database error, unavailable PID/process or invalid PID
returns HTTP 503 with `{"status": "unavailable"}`. HEAD has the corresponding
status and headers without a response body. Process existence does not establish
queue progress or provider email delivery; those require live verification.

#### `POST /api/invitations/accept/` (US-04)

Public: anonymous visitors and every signed-in role may accept a valid invitation.
The invitation token authorizes the operation; callers cannot choose the email,
name, role or store in the request. Signed-in sessions must send `X-CSRFToken`.
Acceptance creates a new active user from the invitation and sets a password using
the configured sign-up validators. An email already registered to an active or
inactive user is refused case-insensitively; no existing account is overwritten.

Request (JSON): `{"token": "<invitation token>", "password": "<new password>"}`.
Success is HTTP 200 with `{"accepted": true}`. Acceptance does not sign in the
new user or switch an existing browser session.

Errors follow the `{ "code", "message", "fields" }` convention, with French and
English messages:

| Status | Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invitation_invalid` | The token is malformed or unknown. |
| 400 | `invitation_expired` | The saved invitation expiry has been reached. |
| 400 | `invitation_used` | The invitation has already been accepted. |
| 400 | `email_already_registered` | The invited email already belongs to an account. |
| 400 | `validation_error` | Password or request validation failed. |
| 503 | `invitation_unavailable` | Service availability error mapping. |

Signed-in requests without valid CSRF protection receive 403; unsupported methods
receive 405. Failed acceptance does not create a user or consume the invitation.
Lifetime configuration is checked by the creation service; existing invitations
are accepted against their saved expiry without re-reading that configuration.
The public `/invitation/:token` page (#431) submits the token and password;
password confirmation remains in the form. Anonymous success opens `/sign-in`.
Signed-in visitors see completion guidance and keep their session until they
explicitly sign out using the existing public header control.
US-13 partner approval/reissue now calls account issuance and the US-57 queued
notification service. Other staff/store-team issuing endpoints and household
linking remain with US-05, US-06 and US-18. Invitation acceptance does not send
another invitation.

#### Admin store management (US-14)

Admin only, with the same access and error envelope as the partner review below:
401 signed out, 403 for every other role and inactive admins, 404 for an unknown
store. Rules BR-STORE-001 to BR-STORE-006 are in
[business-rules.md](../02-requirements/business-rules.md#store-administration-us-14).

| Request | Success | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/staff/stores/?q=ontario&status=active&page=1` | 200 page of stores by name, with `open_listings` per row and `counts: {all, active, inactive}` for the same search | 400 `validation_error` for an unknown `status` |
| `GET /api/staff/stores/{id}/` | 200 store with every field, `opening_hours` (see below), `is_badr`, `is_active`, `can_change_status` (false for the B.A.D.R. store; the screen shows the status switch from it), and the deactivation preview `open_listings` and `households_to_notify` (households with an email that would be told, counted once each) | 404 |
| `PATCH /api/staff/stores/{id}/` with only the fields to change | 200 store; one `update` audit event with the changed field names, none when nothing changed | 400 `validation_error`: any field error, or "This field cannot be changed." for `id`, `is_badr`, `application`, `is_active`, timestamps or unknown keys |
| `POST /api/staff/stores/{id}/deactivate/` `{ "reason": "..." }` | 200 store plus `listings_cancelled` and `reservations_cancelled` | 400 `store_is_badr`; 400 `validation_error` on `reason`; 409 `store_already_inactive` |
| `POST /api/staff/stores/{id}/reactivate/` `{ "reason": "..." }` | 200 store | 400 `validation_error` on `reason`; 409 `store_already_active` |

Editable fields: `name`, `street_number`, `street_name`, `unit`, `city`,
`postal_code`, `phone` (E.164), `email` (the store's contact address, never the
manager's sign-in email), `opening_hours` and `pickup_instructions`. Blank `unit`
and `pickup_instructions` are stored as `null`.

`opening_hours` holds `mon` to `sun`, each `{ "open": "HH:MM", "close": "HH:MM" }`
or `null`, plus a read-only `notes` with the free text from a partner application
(or `null`). A `null` day means closed only once the weekly schedule is filled in:
a store approved from an application (only `notes`) or the B.A.D.R. placeholder
(`{}`) has no schedule yet, so every day comes back `null` without meaning closed.
When all seven days are `null`, treat the hours as not set. A PATCH must send all
seven days, with at least one open; `notes` is kept.

#### Staff review of partner applications (US-13)

Admin only: an active account with the `admin` role. Anonymous requests get 401;
every other role, and inactive admins, get 403. Errors use the
`{ "code", "message", "fields" }` envelope.

| Request | Success | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/staff/partner-applications/?status=submitted&page=1&page_size=20` | 200 page of applications, oldest first; without `status`, every status | 400 `validation_error` for an unknown `status` |
| `POST /api/staff/partner-applications/{id}/approve/` (no body) | 200 application with `status: "approved"`; store, store-manager invitation and audit event saved in one transaction, shared approval email queued after commit | 404 unknown ID; 409 `application_already_decided` |
| `POST /api/staff/partner-applications/{id}/reject/` `{ "reason": "..." }` | 200 application with `status: "rejected"` and the trimmed `decision_reason`; audit event saved, stored reason included in the shared rejection email queued after commit | 400 `validation_error` on `reason` (missing, blank or over 500 characters); 404; 409 `application_already_decided` |

Both emails use the applicant's saved language and US-57 delivery metadata/retry
handling. Invitation URLs use `PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN`; no separate frontend-origin
setting is required. A successful decision response does not establish provider
acceptance or inbox delivery. Operator reissue retains the original decision and
queues a new invitation; stale queued links are checked before transport as
described in [the notification runbook](../../backend/modules/notifications/README.md#one-use-links-and-cleanup).

Each application returns `id`, `status`, `can_decide`, the business fields (`business_name`,
`business_type`, `neq`, `website`, address fields), the contact fields
(`contact_first_name`, `contact_last_name`, `contact_role`, `contact_email`,
`contact_phone`), `goods_categories`, `expected_frequency`, `opening_hours`,
`message`, `language`, `decision_reason`, `decided_at` and `created_at` (UTC).
`can_decide` is computed by the backend from active-admin access and submitted
state. Clients render this flag; services recheck the same rule under the lock.
The decisions are made by `services.approve_application` and
`services.reject_application`; see the [stores module](../../backend/modules/stores/README.md).

#### `POST /api/partner-applications/` (US-12)

Public: no account, anonymous visitors and every role may submit. A signed-in
session must still send `X-CSRFToken`. Rate-limited to **5 requests per hour per
client IP address**, shared by anonymous and signed-in callers; a port in the
forwarded address is ignored. Every request that reaches the endpoint counts,
including those refused with 400 or 409. A signed-in session refused for a missing
CSRF token (403) is stopped before the limit and is not counted; it saves nothing.
Messages use the request's language: Django's `django_language` cookie if it holds
French or English, otherwise `Accept-Language`, otherwise French. That language is
also stored as the language of the contact's emails. The Iris frontend sends
`Accept-Language` and does not set the cookie.

Request (JSON). Fields and rules are those of the
[partner application form](../02-requirements/forms-and-fields.md#partner-application-form);
optional fields may be empty or omitted. Any other field, such as `status`, is refused.

```json
{
  "business_name": "Boulangerie Exemple",
  "business_type": "bakery",
  "neq": "",
  "website": "exemple.ca",
  "street_number": "1234",
  "street_name": "rue Saint-Denis",
  "unit": "",
  "city": "Montréal",
  "postal_code": "H2X 1Y4",
  "contact_first_name": "Alex",
  "contact_last_name": "Exemple",
  "contact_role": "",
  "contact_email": "nom@exemple.ca",
  "contact_phone": "+15145550123",
  "goods_categories": ["bakery", "dairy_eggs"],
  "expected_frequency": "weekly",
  "opening_hours": "lun-ven 9 h-18 h",
  "message": "",
  "consent_contact": true
}
```

`goods_categories` holds codes from `GET /api/categories/`. `contact_phone` is
stored in E.164, as produced by the shared `PhoneField`. Direct requests also
accept ten national digits, optional `1`/`+1`, and familiar phone punctuation;
the backend normalizes before checking canonical lengths. Postal codes accept
lowercase/unspaced input and whitespace, returning uppercase with one space in
stored records. Partner and walk-in fields use the same contact rules documented
in [forms-and-fields.md](../02-requirements/forms-and-fields.md#shared-rules).

| Status | Body |
| --- | --- |
| 201 | `{"id", "status": "submitted", "created_at"}`; no personal data is echoed. The contact gets the `partner_application_received` email after the commit. |
| 400 | `{"code": "validation_error", "message", "fields": {"<field>": ["…"]}}` |
| 409 | `{"code": "application_already_open", "message", "fields": {}}`: an application with this email is still `submitted`; the message is the form spec's "already in progress" text with the email. |
| 429 | `{"code": "throttled", "message", "fields": {}}` |
| 405 | Any method other than POST. |

Admins see submitted applications, read-only, in the Django admin until the
US-13 staff screens exist.

### Listings and reservations

US-33 adds the posting backend and US-34 its safety checks (food best-before
date, prohibited categories, the safe-and-allowed confirmation). Photo storage
is implemented through the configured private Azure/Azurite adapter; see the
[posting implementation and handoff](../guides/listing-posting.md).

US-36 adds browsing. `GET /api/listings/` returns the listings an approved
household can see (BR-LIST-004), sorted by pickup start. Pages are always 20
cards: only `?page=` is read, and `page_size` is ignored (#506). Filters:
`category` (a category code), `store` (a store ID) and `today=true` (can still
be picked up today, Montreal time; BR-LIST-005). Leave out an unused filter.
Signed out gets 401; any other role, or a household that is not approved
(code `household_not_approved`), gets 403. Tiers do not exist yet (US-51), so
every approved household sees every visible listing. Cards include nullable
`photo_url`: a read-only link for one private blob that expires within five
minutes. Internal photo references are not returned. Responses containing links
use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. If storage configuration or signing
fails, the authorized listing details remain available with `photo_url: null`;
the backend logs a safe event and never substitutes a public URL.
The view is in reservations, the module
allowed to read both households and listings.

US-41 adds reserving. `POST /api/reservations/` with `{listing_id, quantity}`
(quantity 1 to 10, default 1) reserves for the signed-in household and answers
201 with `{id, listing_id, quantity, pickup_code, status, created_at}`.
Errors use `{code, message, fields}`: 400 `validation_error` or
`quantity_over_listing_limit`; 401 signed out; 403 other roles or
`household_not_approved`; 404 `listing_not_available` (closed, cancelled,
ended, unknown, or not visible to the household); 409 `sold_out`,
`not_enough_units` or `too_many_active_reservations`; 503
`reservations_unavailable` (no `reservations` rule in effect) or
`pickup_code_unavailable`. Rules BR-RES-006 to BR-RES-010. US-41 also adds
`max_per_household` to each `GET /api/listings/` card, so the listing screen can
show the household limit and the quantity picker.

| Method   | Path                                       | Who                  | Purpose                                          | Status  |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------- |
| GET      | `/api/listings/?category=&store=&today=`   | Approved beneficiary | Visible listings (tier timing applied)           | Implemented (US-36); tier timing waits for US-51 |
| GET      | `/api/listings/{id}/`                      | Approved beneficiary | Listing detail                                   | Planned |
| GET/POST | `/api/store/listings/`                     | Store staff          | Own store's listings; post a listing             | POST implemented, including private photos; GET planned |
| GET      | `/api/store/listings/categories/`          | Store staff          | Categories the store may post in (prohibited ones left out) | Implemented |
| PATCH    | `/api/store/listings/{id}/`                | Store staff          | Edit (quantity ≥ reserved)                       | Planned |
| POST     | `/api/store/listings/{id}/cancel/`         | Store staff          | Cancel; reservations cancelled without strikes   | Planned |
| POST     | `/api/reservations/`                       | Approved beneficiary | `{listing_id, quantity}` → reservation with code | Implemented (US-41) |
| GET      | `/api/reservations/me/?status=`            | Beneficiary          | My reservations and history                      | Planned |
| POST     | `/api/reservations/{id}/cancel/`           | Beneficiary          | Cancel                                           | Planned |
| GET      | `/api/store/pickups/?date=`                | Store staff          | Today's expected pickups                         | Planned |
| POST     | `/api/store/pickups/lookup/`               | Store staff          | `{code}` → who and what                          | Implemented (US-44); `{qr}` waits for the QR format (US-42) |
| POST     | `/api/store/pickups/{id}/confirm/`         | Store staff          | Mark picked up                                   | Implemented (US-44) |
| POST     | `/api/store/pickups/{id}/problem/`         | Store staff          | Report a problem (opens a review case)           | Planned |

The two pickup endpoints (US-44) accept `store_staff` and `store_manager`
accounts assigned to a store, with the session cookie and CSRF token.
Signed out gets 401; other signed-in roles get 403. Lookup takes
`{"code": "…"}` (spaces and lowercase accepted; the scan screen sends the
decoded QR text the same way) and changes nothing. Confirm has no body. Both
return the pickup as
`{"id", "status", "holder", "alternate", "title", "unit", "quantity",
"pickup_code", "pickup_start", "pickup_end", "picked_up_at"}`, where `holder`
and `alternate` are a first name and last initial or `null`
(BR-RES-001 to BR-RES-005).

| Status | Body |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | The pickup. After confirm, `status` is `picked_up` and `picked_up_at` is set. |
| 400 | `{"code": "validation_error", "message", "fields": {"code": ["…"]}}` |
| 401 | `{"code": "not_authenticated", "message", "fields": {}}` |
| 403 | `{"code": "permission_denied", "message", "fields": {}}` |
| 404 | `{"code": "unknown_code"}` (lookup) or `{"code": "unknown_reservation"}` (confirm: not at this store), with `message` and `fields: {}` |
| 409 | `{"code", "message", "fields": {}}` with `wrong_store`, `ambiguous_code`, `already_picked_up` (adds `picked_up_at`, the first confirmation), `cancelled`, `no_show`, `not_open_yet` or `window_ended` |
